title: Ben Johnson on Week 5 loss | Press Conference
headline: Bears QB situation in flux: Tyson Bagent was benched for Case Keenum after his second interception, and Caleb Williams is 'on track' and 'close' to returning for Atlanta, though Johnson wouldn't commit to Week 6.
summary: Johnson said the Bears' Week 5 loss in Green Bay came down to things that worked in their three wins not showing up: five offensive turnovers (three Bagent interceptions), poor execution in both the run and pass game, and four 40+ yard pass plays allowed on defense. He took blame for the offensive struggles, including the early run game and play-calling, and credited Jonathan Gannon's defense for keeping Chicago off balance. Bagent was pulled for Case Keenum after the second interception because Johnson wanted a spark and Bagent never found rhythm. Caleb Williams practiced Friday and worked out Sunday morning; Johnson called him 'on track' and said a return for Atlanta is close but not certain. He wouldn't say whether Bagent or Keenum would start in Week 6 if Williams can't go, saying the staff will decide this week. Injuries of note are a hamstring for a player whose name was garbled (likely Tyrique Stevenson, unconfirmed), a hamstring for T.J. Edwards, and a quad for Dayo Odeyingbo, all to be evaluated Monday. Johnson said the process doesn't change and said he believes in the staff and players. He suggested the offense could look to stretch the field more going forward.

injuries.detail: Hamstring injury suffered in the game; to be evaluated tomorrow.
Quad injury suffered in the game; to be evaluated tomorrow.
Back at practice Friday and worked out Sunday morning; Johnson said he's on track and a return for Atlanta is close but uncertain.

signals.claim: Williams could return for Week 6 at Atlanta, but it may be after that.
signals.note: Williams' availability for Week 6 is uncertain, so keep him on your radar and check practice reports.

signals.claim: Bagent was benched after his second interception and is not assured of starting if Williams is out in Week 6.
signals.note: Bagent threw three interceptions and was pulled, so he's a poor fantasy option and his starting job is uncertain.
signals.quote: It was Tyson just could never feel like he got in a rhythm

signals.claim: Keenum came in after Bagent's second interception and could start in Week 6 if Williams can't play.
signals.note: If Williams misses Week 6, Keenum could be in the QB mix, which affects Bears pass catchers.

topics.detail: Five offensive turnovers and poor execution in the run and pass game sank the offense. Johnson put the early run-game struggles and play-calling on himself.
Chicago allowed four passes of 40+ yards and gave up chunk completions behind the secondary, including a bad angle on a long touchdown on third and 22.
Johnson called it a fast group with active safeties, a strong nickel, and a communicating linebacker who made adjustments at the line.
Johnson said the horizontal attack wasn't unusual, but the offense can look to stretch the field more going forward.

title: Zac Taylor Recaps Win over Miami | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals beat Miami 31-24 and head into the bye at 3-2. Samaje Perine had the hot hand in the run game, and Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins played through injury designations.
summary: Zac Taylor was glad to win a tight game but frustrated with the sloppiness. He listed two personal fouls, two red-zone fumbles, a kickoff caught at the 4-yard line, a field-goal penalty that led to a Miami touchdown, and over 200 rushing yards allowed. He said the bye comes at a great time for a worn-out team after three down-to-the-wire games and a brutally hot day. He praised the run game and the linemen's practice week, and said Perine finished runs well while he still has a lot of confidence in Chase Brown. Taylor described the volume of runs as how the game played out, because Miami gave up underneath throws and light boxes, not as a planned blueprint. Boye Mafe got praise for relentless energy, run-game physicality and pass-rush impact. Ja'Marr Chase cleared concussion protocol on Saturday, and Tee Higgins insisted on playing after Taylor wanted to see him practice. Joe Burrow only jammed the thumb on his non-throwing hand. Tanner Hudson was called dependable for filling in at tight end whenever Erick All or Mike Gesicki leave the field. Next up is Baltimore in two weeks, and Taylor warned that the mobile quarterback there can hurt them the way Miami's did.

injuries.detail: Questionable going into the game. Cleared concussion protocol on Saturday and played, making plays.
Questionable going into the game. Taylor needed to see him practice, and he did, then played and made plays.
Appeared to have a wrap on his left hand. Taylor said he jammed the thumb on his non-throwing hand and called it nothing, just a little bandage.

signals.claim: Perine's strong run-game finishing could earn him continued run-game work alongside Chase Brown.
signals.note: Perine appears to have had the hot hand in a run-heavy win, but Taylor framed the backfield split loosely, so treat the touch share as unsettled.
Taylor called him one of two great backs and said the touch split can go either way, so his share may fluctuate with game flow.
signals.quote: Got a lot of confidence in Chase.

signals.claim: Mafe will keep a significant role as an edge rusher and run defender.
signals.note: Good for his IDP value: strong game, praised for pass-rush impact and physicality.
signals.quote: Does a great job affecting the passer.

signals.claim: Chase cleared concussion protocol and is healthy enough to play, with the bye week coming.
signals.note: The injury concern appears resolved and he gets extra rest before Baltimore.
signals.quote: Jamaar had to clear protocol, I think, on Saturday.

signals.claim: Higgins practiced, played through his injury and produced.
signals.note: He was questionable but Taylor praised his toughness, and the bye gives him time to recover.
signals.quote: I need to see him do it, you know, in practice.

signals.claim: Burrow's jammed thumb on his non-throwing hand is not a concern.
signals.note: Minor and not on his throwing hand, with the bye week to recover.

signals.claim: Hudson will keep filling in at tight end when Erick All or Mike Gesicki leave the field.
signals.note: Taylor trusts him in every tight end role, but he is a depth piece with limited fantasy value unless a tight end is hurt.

topics.detail: Taylor listed two personal fouls, two red-zone fumbles, a kickoff caught on the 4-yard line and a field-goal penalty that gave Miami a touchdown. He said the team is better than that and has plenty to clean up.
Cincinnati allowed over 200 rushing yards, partly because of big quarterback runs. Taylor said they have to do a better job, especially since they face a quarterback in two weeks who can do the same.
Taylor said the run volume was how the game played out, with Miami dropping into shells and giving up underneath throws, not a planned blueprint. He will take the offense game to game.
He said the bye comes at the right time for a tired team after three close games and one of the hottest October games in Miami history. He praised the players for battling through it.
Taylor said he needs the defense to decide who Hudson is, meaning whether they will be in base or nickel when he is on the field.

title: DeMeco Ryans on First Win, Will Anderson Jr. & C.J. Stroud | Full Q&A
headline: Texans got their first win over the Titans, but David Montgomery has a groin injury and may miss time, and Ryans appeared to confirm Marvin Harrison Jr. was acquired by trade.
summary: Ryans was happy to get the first win after a difficult start and said all three phases played complementary football. The offense controlled the game, though self-inflicted penalties stalled a couple of red-zone drives that ended in field goals. He praised C.J. Stroud for his decisions, his rushing touchdown and his year-two comfort and command at the line. The defense created turnovers, and Will Anderson Jr. had three sacks while being moved around the line, including inside. Azeez Al-Shaair's return was highlighted as a stabilizing presence in the middle, and Reed Blankenship was praised for his physical play and growing comfort in coverage. On injuries, Montgomery has a groin injury and may miss time, and a second player's shoulder is still being evaluated. Tank Dell is back practicing and Ryans is hopeful he returns to game action. Asked about trade rumors, Ryans first dodged the question, then said they traded for Marvin Harrison.

injuries.detail: Groin injury still being evaluated; Ryans said he may miss some time.
Shoulder injury still being looked at to determine how significant it is.
Back on the practice field; his progress this week will determine his availability, and Ryans is hopeful he returns to game action.
Back in the lineup and praised as the defense's communicator and field general.

signals.claim: Montgomery may miss time with a groin injury.
signals.note: His availability is in doubt, so fantasy managers should have a backup RB plan until there is more clarity.
signals.quote: He has a groin injury. May miss some time.

signals.claim: Houston has acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. from Arizona via trade.
signals.note: If confirmed, he adds a WR to a thin receiver room and could take targets quickly. The delivery was casual, so check official reports.

signals.claim: Dell may return to game action if his practice progress continues this week.
signals.note: A return would add a WR option, but his status depends on how the week goes.
signals.quote: happy to see tank back out on the field practicing

signals.claim: Anderson will keep being moved across the defensive line, on the edge and inside, to create pass-rush matchups.
signals.note: A three-sack game plus a flexible rush role supports his sack upside for IDP.
signals.quote: So to see him go out and dominate the game by getting three sacks

signals.claim: Stroud will continue to lead the offense with more command and pre-snap control in year two.
signals.note: Ryans praised his decision-making and comfort, and his rushing touchdown adds some rushing upside.
signals.quote: You see his comfort level. You see his confidence. You see his command

signals.claim: Al-Shaair is back in the starting middle linebacker role, running the defense's communication.
signals.note: His return should bring back his tackle volume for IDP leagues.
signals.quote: Aziz is our field general. He's our communicator.

signals.claim: Blankenship is becoming more comfortable in coverage and should keep making plays.
signals.note: His improved comfort and physical style point to more IDP production at safety.
signals.quote: I just love the physical style, which Reed plays with

topics.detail: Ryans said the O-line played well and the run game was good despite a couple of big runs called back. The line allowed only one sack.

The defense took the ball away, with Jake Hansen getting a takeaway and Dominique Robinson forcing a fumble the team recovered. Ryans credited the D-line's pressure for giving the DBs more freedom in coverage.
Ryans credited offensive coordinator Kelly (name as captioned) for mixing up the offense and said Stroud's growth has raised the level of the players around him.
Second halves had been a weakness this season, but the team finished the game well. Red-zone penalties cost them touchdowns in the first half.

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Broncos
headline: Harbaugh took full blame for a failed fourth-and-1 at the 41 in a loss that drops LAC to 0-5; Slater and several other offensive linemen and receivers are out, and he gave no timeline for the linemen's return before Kansas City.
summary: Harbaugh opened by saying going for it on fourth-and-1 at the 41-yard line was the wrong decision. He said he was never angrier at himself and takes 100% accountability for swinging the game's momentum. He praised the team's effort across offense, defense and special teams, and said the defense produced multiple three-and-outs, a big turnover and sudden-change stops. He said the offense is improving, pointing to touchdown drives against one of the league's top defenses and to the young offensive linemen, who he said acquitted themselves well. The team started four rookie offensive linemen and was without Rashawn Slater and other players, and receivers are thin. Asked about Justin Herbert's late turnovers and his five straight games with a turnover, he blamed the situations his decisions put Herbert in, such as having to throw on fourth-and-6. Asked whether the lineman would be back for Kansas City, he said he didn't know. He offered no scheme or play-calling changes and said the plan is to stay the course, work hard and get the critical coaching decisions right.

injuries.detail: Missing the Denver game; Harbaugh gave no return timeline and said he didn't know if the linemen would be back for Kansas City.

signals.claim: Harbaugh blames the coaching decision, not Herbert, for the late turnovers and the five-game turnover streak.
signals.note: Herbert is turning it over weekly behind a patchwork offensive line, but Harbaugh is backing him publicly and not changing the plan.

signals.claim: Slater and other offensive linemen may or may not return for the Kansas City game; no timeline given.
signals.note: Without Slater the line stays young and thin, which hurts pass protection and the run game for the whole offense.
signals.quote: I don't know. We'll we'll see.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said he should have called timeout and punted after seeing the defense gap down on fourth-and-1 at the 41. He called it the turning point and said he put the team in a bad position.
LAC started four rookie offensive linemen because Slater and others were out, and Harbaugh praised them for helping produce touchdown drives.
At 0-5, Harbaugh said he has no special message beyond fighting hard and said he will stay the course with no major offensive changes.
He praised the defense for multiple three-and-outs, a big turnover and sudden-change stops.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 11, 2026
headline: Sirianni owned the late kickoff decision in the 19-17 London loss to Jacksonville and admitted the second-half offense has to be fixed, but he gave no player-specific fantasy news.
summary: Sirianni opened by taking full blame for the 19-17 loss to Jacksonville. He said he made the wrong decision on the end-of-game kickoff (not kicking it out of bounds) and declined to explain the reasoning or whether he followed the pre-set process. He praised the defense for keeping Philadelphia in the game and said the offense did enough late to win it. He explained that the offense ran the ball at the end hoping for a first down so it could call a timeout with about five seconds left, but Jacksonville stopped it and held its timeouts. He said kneeling to run the clock was possible but risked losing two to four yards on a long field goal. He acknowledged the offense has struggled in the second half after good first halves, said the team played a little differently today, and said the coaches must look at themselves first and figure out how to finish games. He said injuries to personnel did not affect the kickoff coverage, and that he has total faith in everyone on the field. He called the team mentally and physically tough and praised the London atmosphere and traveling fans. He also noted that the team lost many key players this week, though he did not name them.

signals.note: Made a standout tackle on a Jaguars tight end at the end of the first half, a sign of defensive energy. It carries little fantasy value except for IDP leagues.

topics.detail: Sirianni said he made the wrong decision by not kicking the ball out of bounds, put it fully on himself, and refused to detail the reasoning or whether he followed the pre-set process. Jacksonville returned the kick and then hit the winning field goal.

Sirianni said the offense has been strong in the first half but has struggled to close games in the second. He said the coaches must examine how they put players in position to succeed and called it something that will keep hurting them if not fixed.

The offense ran the ball at the end hoping for a first down, which would have allowed a timeout with about five seconds left. Jacksonville stopped the run and still had its timeouts. Sirianni said kneeling to bleed the clock would have cost yardage on a long field goal attempt.

Sirianni said the team dealt with speculation about giving up on the season and the loss of many key players. He said the team is together and tough, and that injuries did not affect the kickoff coverage unit.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/11/26
headline: Jayden Daniels returned and played sharp in a 'gutting' tie; Quinn took blame for the end-of-game clock mismanagement and flagged secondary and defensive late-game collapses.
summary: Quinn opened by calling the game a hard-fought tie that feels like a loss, and took full responsibility for the final sequence, saying he should have clocked the ball earlier rather than trying to gain more yards for a kick. He said Jayden Daniels was not at fault for the sequencing, noting it was either an out-of-bounds throw or a clock and that it was his call. Quinn praised Daniels in his return, citing his work at the line of scrimmage against blitzes, his smart use of his legs without forcing plays, and accurate throws in crunch time to Terry McLaurin and another target (transcribed as 'Burke'). The defense held up through much of the third quarter but then allowed three straight touchdown drives, which Quinn attributed to failing to close out when the opponent was in hurry-up mode and to being unable to stop scrambling plays or cover premium tight ends and receivers. He said the team was dealing with injuries at receiver and safety coming off the London trip, and praised how players prepared despite uncertainty about who would be available. He said he hadn't yet reviewed the penalties (including Amik Robertson's goal-line pass interference) or the early pre-snap flags. He said the team will keep practicing two-minute situations and is resilient after five games of adversity.

injuries.detail: Not an injury; he was flagged for goal-line pass interference, which Quinn hadn't reviewed yet.

signals.claim: Daniels is back on the field and looked sharp after missing time.
signals.note: A healthy, effective Daniels who used his legs selectively and delivered in crunch time is a strong sign for the WAS passing game and his fantasy floor.
signals.quote: I thought for somebody that's missed time I thought he played sharp.

signals.claim: McLaurin is a go-to target in crunch-time moments, with Daniels delivering the ball to him in the right location.
signals.note: Quinn singled him out as a late-game connection with Daniels, supporting his target share and reliability.

topics.detail: Quinn said he should have called a clock early and kicked instead of trying to gain more yards after the first-down run; he called it his responsibility alone and said the team will keep drilling two-minute situations.
The defense allowed three straight touchdown drives late after a strong third quarter, failing to close out. Quinn pointed to scrambling plays and premium opposing tight ends and receivers as issues.
The team dealt with injuries at receiver and safety coming off London, and Quinn praised players for preparing despite uncertainty about availability.
Quinn wants to review the early pre-snap penalties and hasn't assessed the Robertson pass interference call yet.
Quinn praised a player (transcribed as 'pain') for an incredible forced fumble in overtime that gave the team a chance.
